intensify

/in-TEN-sih-fy/ - the stress falls on TEN · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Intensify means to become or make stronger or more extreme.

As the town-hall hour wore on, the questions intensified — polite curiosity hardening into cross-examination.

Example

When the kayaker missed his evening check-in, the search intensified by the hour: two boats became nine, flashlights gave way to floodlights, and the sweep tightened from guesswork to fifty-meter lanes. By midnight the river mouth was lit bright as noon.

Intensify is the exact verb because the effort didn't just grow — it grew stronger and more concentrated. Growth can mean covering more area; intensifying turns the dial. Heat, pressure, rivalries, searches: whenever the degree itself climbs, intensify is the word.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

heighten: Heighten means to raise the level of something you can sense — tension, awareness, color — so it registers a notch more sharply. Intensify claims more than a raised level: the force itself grows stronger and more concentrated, its own dial turning toward the extreme. Heightened is a louder notch; intensify is a hotter fire.

deepen: Deepen means to grow more firmly rooted and more deeply felt, often with less show on the surface, not more. Intensify pushes the other direction: the degree itself climbs toward the extreme, where everyone can see it. Grief deepens over quiet years; a storm can only intensify.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

subside: sink back toward calm

slacken: lose tightness and force

Where it sits · how sharply the force is rising

mount → intensify → erupt

mount vs. intensify: Pressure mounts by quiet accumulation; intensify says more — the force itself is climbing in strength, not just piling up.

erupt vs. intensify: Erupt is the ladder's far end: what has been intensifying finally bursts every limit at once.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-: toward

Root — tens-: stretched (Latin tendere)

Suffix — -ify: to make

Put it together: In- (toward) + tens- (stretched — Latin tendere) + -ify (to make) = to make stretched tighter. Latin intensus described the drawn bowstring. Intensify keeps the image: whatever intensifies — heat, pressure, a search — is being stretched tauter, notch by notch.

Use the root in a new word: tension: You could feel the tension in the locker room before the deciding shootout.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Intensify is the degree verb: heat, pain, pressure, rivalry — the thing itself climbs in strength, and it can do so on its own ('the argument intensified'). Amplify, a unit-mate, usually has an amplifier: something strengthens a sound or feeling. Magnify changes only how big a thing looks. When the dial itself is turning up, intensify.
